source.title: Transformers Linearly Represent Highly Structured World Models

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes dedicated neurons in a Sudoku solver, but does not test whether neurons respond to unrelated input types, nor any listed version's specific claim. Its neuron findings are related to the topic but do not assess polysemanticity or its prevalence.
record.gate_note: The paper reports specific, monosemantic naked-single detector neurons and their causal effects. These findings concern neuron function, but the study does not measure mixed responses to unrelated inputs or test the listed versions. Background references to prior work are not results from this study.
record.test_reason: An 8-layer transformer trained on Sudoku traces, with probing and circuit analysis. The paper calls 91 selected final-MLP neurons 'monosemantic', but it never measures how many neurons respond to unrelated inputs. It studies no image classifier or natural-language model, and makes no comparison of causes, architectures or measurement choices. None of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors also conclude that the model represents the board by substructure (rows, columns, boxes) rather than by cell, and that mid-layer attention heads act as substructure-local constraint checkers.
record.recipe_differences: This is a Sudoku world-model and circuit analysis using linear probes, activation patching, attention analysis, and direct logit attribution; it does not apply a polysemantic-neuron measurement or intervention from the original sources to test mixed neuron responses.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe results vary by layer: the substructure representation appears at layer 4, while cell-level results differ across layers. Fixed-threshold probe accuracy also changes across solving positions, whereas AUC remains near 1.0 for layers 4–7.

fits_no_version.finding: A cutoff-selected set of 91 final-MLP neurons in a Sudoku transformer responds specifically to naked-single states of particular cells. Ablating them drops the target logit by 11.4 while barely changing another naked-single placement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small transformers trained on structured algorithmic tasks can contain sparse, cell-specific, apparently monosemantic detector neurons in the final MLP.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code is available at a link, but no URL is present in the supplied text.
record.problems: The neuron analysis concerns one architecture trained on one puzzle type. The paper does not test different architectures, training setups, or mixed-response prevalence; its detector neurons are selected using an activation-gap cutoff.

untested.parts: No language model. The Sudoku-trace transformer's neurons were not surveyed for mixed responses, and no layer-wise share is reported.
Superposition and feature-versus-neuron capacity are not examined.
Initialization, regularization and training noise are not examined.
Only one GELU architecture and one training setup; no comparison.
Canonical polysemantic neurons are not revisited.
No comparison of activation ranges or scoring methods.

record.verdict_notes: The study uses 'monosemantic' descriptively, for neurons selected by a cutoff; it did not screen neurons for polysemanticity. The rest of the paper (probes, attention heads) is unrelated to the claim. The record's reader relation (discusses, T6) and its 'none' row links are kept.

versions.untested_parts: No image classifier or vision neuron responses are studied.
No transformer language-model MLP neuron responses to tokens or contexts are studied.
The study does not test feature capacity, superposition, or whether features outnumber neurons.
The study does not test initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity.

Only one model architecture and training setup are studied; there is no comparison of activation functions, architectures, or regularization, nor a polysemanticity rate or associated performance cost.
The study does not revisit canonical polysemantic neurons or test whether their mixed responses arise from a shared feature. It identifies dedicated neurons for a specific Sudoku behavior.
The study does not compare methods or scoring choices for classifying neuron polysemanticity.

rows.subject: 8-layer transformer (Sudoku model; model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Measured final-MLP neuron activation conditioned on candidate count for each cell; selected neurons with activation gap above 3.0.
rows.measure: Number and cell coverage of identified naked-single detector neurons; the paper says they fire exclusively for their associated cell's naked-single state and otherwise remain unactivated.
rows.value: 91 neurons; 71 cells had one associated neuron and 10 cells had two.
rows.note: The authors describe these selected neurons as dedicated and monosemantic. The result is about a specific Sudoku circuit, not a sample of neurons tested for unrelated mixed responses.
rows.check: The 91-neuron count is a selection result: it comes from an activation-gap cutoff of 3.0 applied to all cell-neuron pairs. The 'fire exclusively' claim is the authors' statement, shown only for one example neuron (Fig. 5). Neuron responses outside candidate-count conditions were not checked. This is not a polysemanticity rate, so the row is not evidence on any version.

rows.subject: 8-layer transformer (Sudoku model; model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Projected the output weights of the 91 identified neurons through the unembedding matrix to measure their logit contributions when firing.

conditions.value: placement tokens for the neuron-associated cell
placement tokens for the other 80 empty cells

rows.measure: Mean logit contribution from the neuron output weights.
rows.value: Target-cell placement tokens: mean +3.00 logits (σ = 0.10 in Section 5.2; Table 5 reports target mean 3.00 and target std 0.11). Other empty cells: mean −0.02 in Section 5.2; Table 5 reports other mean −0.03.
rows.uncertainty: σ = 0.10 in Section 5.2; Table 5 reports standard deviations 0.11 for target and 0.03 for other cells.
rows.note: The paper says the boost is approximately digit-uniform and negligible for other empty cells. The slight difference between the reported other-cell means is preserved as stated in the two locations.

rows.subject: 8-layer transformer (Sudoku model; model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Mean-ablated the naked-single neuron(s) associated with the cell the model was about to predict.

conditions.value: correct digit for the selected naked-single cell

rows.measure: Drop in target placement-token logit, clean minus ablated.
rows.baseline: clean run; mean clean logit not stated for this comparison
rows.note: The text rounds the drop to 11.4.

rows.operation_detail: Mean-ablated the naked-single neuron(s) associated with one cell and measured the effect on the other naked-single placement on the same board.

conditions.value: other simultaneous naked-single placement on the same board

rows.note: The negative clean-minus-ablated value means the other placement's logit increased by 0.655 under ablation; the text describes this as barely affecting the other cell.
